title: március 15., augusztus 20., október 23.: The National Holidays

sections.title: Hungary's three national holidays
sections.content: A *nemzeti ünnep* is a national holiday, and Hungary has three big ones. *Március 15.* remembers the revolution of 1848: people wear a red-white-green badge, the *kokárda* (you know the colours from A1). *Augusztus 20.* is Saint Stephen's Day, the foundation of the state, and there are *tűzijáték* (fireworks) in Budapest. *Október 23.* remembers the revolution of 1956. You know the ordinals from Unit 2: the dot after the number in *március 15.* is read as an ordinal, *március tizenötödike*. When you say "on" that day, you add *-n* as in Unit 2: *március tizenötödikén*.

items.spanish: Március tizenötödikén kokárda van a kabátomon.
items.english: On 15 March there is a cockade on my coat.

items.spanish: Augusztus huszadikán este tűzijáték van Budapesten.
items.english: On 20 August in the evening there are fireworks in Budapest.
23 October is a national holiday too.

sections.content: Name the day itself with *-a/-e* (*március tizenötödike*) and say "on that day" with *-án/-én* (*március tizenötödikén*). In writing, the day number takes a full stop: *március 15.*
